A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. - "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

Start a separate Claude Code session for a task while you stay with the user (when: see "Starting other sessions"). `initiation` says who wants it: "user_asked" starts it now and returns its id; "offer" is for a task the user named in their latest message (new work here, or "suggest / split off / make a task or session for X"): called with a title alone, it shows a "New session" / "Do it here" card and WAITS for their answer, so it must be the only call in that message (no update_plan, no other tool); the result then tells you to carry on here, or to send the brief with proposal_id so the session starts; "own_initiative" is for work you propose yourself that the user has not told you to do — something you noticed, or the follow-up your own answer or work turned up (when your reply calls work a follow-up or a separate PR, propose it here rather than only saying so); the user sees a card and nothing runs until they start it, by clicking it or by telling you (then call this again with just proposal_id).
"user_asked" and "own_initiative" both need a `prompt` — the brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like — and the call is refused without it; `background` does not stand in for it. Only an "offer" is a title alone.
context: "fork" = this whole conversation + your `prompt`. "fresh" (default) = your `prompt` + `background` only, so `background` is required too, at least 80 characters.
Checkout here ("fresh" only): use_worktree false = shares this checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session its branch and PR too: never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); true = its own worktree (the default when this session is in one).
Elsewhere ("fresh", user_asked only, when the user named the place): `cwd`, `target` "ssh" + `host`, `environment` or `preset`; list_start_targets lists the valid names.
Right before calling, write its bold title line and one sentence on what it will do; it has started only once this returns saying so. Never wait for it or poll.

initiation.description: "user_asked": the user asked in words for separate, parallel or background work, or told you to start this piece — it starts now. "offer": a task the user named in their latest message (new work for this session, or one they asked you to suggest, split off or make a session for) — the user is asked first and the call waits for their answer; send only title with it (the brief follows, with proposal_id, if they choose New session). "own_initiative": work you propose yourself that the user has not told you to do — something you noticed, or the follow-up your own answer or work turned up; it waits as a proposal card until the user starts it; never for a task the user's message tells you to do. Required unless proposal_id is set.

proposal_id.description: Start a proposal the user told you to start, exactly as proposed: its task_id and nothing else (wake_when_done may accompany a local one). To change it, dismiss_task it and start a new session.

title.description: Under 60 chars; names the task. Shown on the row or card. Required unless proposal_id is set.

prompt.description: The brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like. Required for "user_asked" and "own_initiative" — the call is refused without it, and `background` does not stand in for it; an "offer" leaves it out (the card shows the user's own message) and you send it with proposal_id once they choose New session.

context.description: "fresh" (default) or "fork" — see the tool description. A "fork" from a worktree session gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip (commit first; uncommitted edits stay here); from a plain checkout it shares the folder.

background.description: Required with "fresh", besides `prompt`: at least 80 characters of overall goal, decisions and constraints so far, how this piece fits — for someone who has not seen this conversation. Ignored for "fork".

wake_when_done.description: Once this session (and any sibling still working) ends its turn, or fails to start (unless it waits at a prompt the user answers there, its folder was never opened in Claude Desktop, or the user started, stopped or archived it), and you are idle, the app continues you, whether or not this is set. true also continues you if this session never gets its task some other way, such as a brief that is not sent; default false; not with own_initiative; ignored with target "cloud", which never continues you.

name.description: Optional short handle for the session ([a-z0-9-], ≤24), e.g. "cli-cleanup". Linked sessions and plan steps refer to it by this name; derived from the title when omitted.

use_worktree.description: "fresh" only (rejected with "fork"). false = shares this session's checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session: its worktree, branch and PR, so never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); not accepted from a session set up to move from the user's checkout into a worktree with EnterWorktree (before or after it moves), one working in a worktree on an SSH host, or one whose worktree was given back. At another place named by `cwd`, `host` or `preset`, false = that folder as it is. true = its own git worktree. Omitted: the same folder when this session works in a plain folder and has never had a worktree (its own, a shared one, or one it will enter later); otherwise its own worktree. Omitted with `preset` or `host`, or with `cwd` from a session on an SSH host: the default set on that preset or SSH connection instead.

model.description: "fresh" only, optional: a cheaper model id for mechanical or read-only pieces (e.g. a Sonnet or Haiku id). Same family or cheaper than yours; anything higher is ignored. Omit to inherit yours.

target.description: "fresh" only. "local" (default) = where this session runs. "cloud" = run it as a cloud session (keeps going when this computer sleeps). Needs the repository on GitHub and a cloud environment — the app checks and tells the user if it cannot, and the task then stays as a card for them to start. It starts from this session's pushed branch when it runs in a worktree, else the repository's default branch. model/effort/use_worktree/cwd/source_branch do not apply. Only when the user asks for the cloud. "ssh" = on the SSH connection named by host (or by a preset).

host.description: With target "ssh": the name of one of the user's saved SSH connections (as list_start_targets reports it) — never a raw hostname, user or key. The app connects as the user configured it and may ask them to sign in.

cwd.description: The folder the session works in, when it is not this project: an absolute (or ~/) path on the host it will run on — this computer, this session's host, or the SSH connection named by host (default there: the connection's folder). Must exist; if the user has not trusted it yet the app asks them first. "fresh" only.

environment.description: With target "cloud": the name or id of one of the user's cloud environments (list_start_targets lists them); omitted = the default one. Self-hosted environments and runner pools need the user's own click and are refused, and so is an environment that cannot run this project's repository.

source_branch.description: The existing local branch the new worktree is cut from. Default in this project: this session's base branch (the one picked when it started, or the one its worktree was cut from). If the session has none and either it runs on an SSH host or its project folder is itself a git worktree or submodule, the folder's current commit. Otherwise, the repository's default branch, or the folder's current commit if that is unknown. Only for a session that gets its own worktree (use_worktree true, or the place's default); not with target "cloud".

branch_name.description: A short slug for the new worktree's branch (the app adds the user's branch prefix and a suffix). Only with a worktree.

preset.description: The name of one of the user's saved session presets on this computer: it names the place itself (a folder here or an SSH connection and folder — do not pass host or cwd with it) and brings model, effort and worktree defaults plus its saved environment variables; use_worktree/model/effort override those. Cloud and Remote Control presets are not available here.

effort.description: "fresh" only, optional: reasoning effort at or below yours. Omit to inherit.

permission_mode.description: Optional, local starts only: the permission mode it starts in — this session's own or a lower one (omit to inherit it). A higher mode, or one the app does not offer here, is refused; raising a session is set_session_permission_mode's card to show.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

## What this is

A 12-hour take-home: a conversational agent over a subject fixed at kickoff, built production-shaped. Python 3.12,
Pydantic AI, FastAPI, Render. Owner: Yarin Ozeri. Reference (same brief, different subject, do not copy): [reference repository name removed].

Subject, data sources and tools: **TODO(kickoff)**. Everything else below is already in place.

## Workflow (Agent OS v3)

- Read `agent-os/product/` (mission, roadmap, tech-stack) before any work; standards in `agent-os/standards/` via `index.yml`.
- One spec per version: `agent-os/specs/<date>-<slug>/spec.md` with Goal, Scope, Acceptance criteria (numbered), Design, Tasks. Use `/shape-spec` in plan mode.
- Every criterion gets `test_criterion_<n>_<slug>`; `tests/test_spec_coverage.py` enforces it.
- Order: spec → code + tests → `uv run ruff check src tests` → `uv run pytest` → eval report if prompts/models changed → README/roadmap closeout → commit.

## House rules

- Comments: one line, ≤100 chars, only when intent is not obvious. Explanations live in `docs/DESIGN.md` and the specs.
- Tests run offline; every external system has a fake. Never patch the network.
- Secrets only via env; never commit `.env`, `data/`, `*.db`. `MODEL_MODE=test` for keyless runs.
- Every AI call goes through Pydantic AI and the budget; no vendor SDK imports outside `app/llm/models.py`.
- Commit messages: `<type>: <what it does>`; tests green first; solo repo, commit straight to `main`.
- Reply in English; keep answers short; surface the size of a change before building it when it grows.

## Commands

```bash
uv sync                      # install
uv run pytest -q             # offline tests
uv run ruff check src tests
uv run agent chat --test "hi"            # offline demo
uv run agent serve                       # http://localhost:8000
uv run agent eval --repeat 3 --tag latest
uv run agent eval --down anthropic --tag anthropic-outage
```

    42	        config=RetryConfig(

     3	Reserve an estimate inside one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction (atomic under concurrency), then settle with the
     4	real cost or release on failure. Over the cap → BudgetExceeded, never a silent downgrade. The provider-side
     5	spend limit is the second line of defence; this ledger is the first.

    53	  input_tokens INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, output_tokens INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    54	  cost_usd REAL NOT NULL, latency_ms INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,

    61	def estimate_cost(prices: dict[str, Price], model: str, input_tokens: int, output_tokens: int) -> float:
    62	    """Price a call from the table; an unknown model is charged the most expensive row (refusing is recoverable)."""
    63	    price = prices.get(model) or prices.get(model.split(":", 1)[-1])
    64	    if price is None:
    65	        price = max(prices.values(), key=lambda p: p.input + p.output) if prices else Price(input=15.0, output=75.0)

    72	    cap_usd: float
    73	    now: Callable[[], datetime] = lambda: datetime.now(UTC)
    74	
    75	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
    76	        if isinstance(self.db_path, Path):
    77	            self.db_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    78	        with self._connect() as conn:
    79	            conn.executescript(_SCHEMA)

    89	    def reserve(self, estimate_usd: float, *, kind: str, model: str) -> str:
    90	        """Hold `estimate_usd` against this month (settled + reserved + failed); BudgetExceeded past the cap."""
    91	        month, rid = self._month(), uuid.uuid4().hex
    92	        with self._connect() as conn:
    93	            conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    94	            spent = conn.execute("SELECT COALESCE(SUM(cost_usd),0) FROM spend WHERE month=?", (month,)).fetchone()[0]
    95	            if spent + estimate_usd > self.cap_usd:
    96	                conn.execute("ROLLBACK")

    98	            conn.execute(
    99	                "INSERT INTO spend VALUES (?,?,?,?,0,0,?,0,'reserved',?)",
   100	                (rid, month, kind, model, estimate_usd, self.now().isoformat()),
   101	            )

   127	                ).fetchone()[0]
   128	            )

=== agent-os/standards/ai-calls.md
# AI calls

- Every model call goes through Pydantic AI (`Agent` with `output_type`). Never import a vendor SDK outside `app/llm/models.py`.
- The answer model is a chain, in `config/agent.yaml` order: same vendor's cheaper model first, then another vendor. `build_chain` drops entries whose key is missing and logs them; with no key at all it fails at startup.
- Three retry layers, each with one job: the httpx transport retries 429/5xx/network per model with Retry-After or exponential backoff (`retry_attempts`, `retry_max_wait_s`); vendor SDK retries are off (`max_retries=0`); `FallbackModel` moves to the next model on `ModelAPIError` or a truncated reply. A timeout counts as a failed attempt and moves on.
- Output is always typed: `AnswerOut` for answers, `Screening` for the guard. A reply that fails validation is retried once with the error, then the turn fails loudly.
- The model never invents facts: every number or name comes from a tool result; `sources` names the tools used; `limitations` says what the data cannot tell.
- `Turn` records which model answered (`served_by`), which failed before it (`failed_attempts`), tokens, cost and latency. The API returns them; evals aggregate them.
- Prompts live in `app/agent/prompts.py` only. Any change to a prompt, the chain, `Screening`, `AnswerOut` or the guard threshold is committed together with a fresh `agent eval` report under `evals/results/`.
- Per-turn ceilings: `UsageLimits(request_limit, cost_limit)` from `config/agent.yaml`; a runaway tool loop stops with `cannot_answer`, not an exception.

# Budget

- Hard monthly cap `BUDGET_USD`, enforced in code before any paid call by `app/llm/budget.py`: reserve an estimate in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction, settle with the real cost after, release on a refusal, keep the estimate charged on a mid-call failure. Over the cap → `budget_exhausted`, never a quiet downgrade.
- Cost per turn comes from Pydantic AI's `RunUsage.cost` (genai-prices). When a model has no price there, `config/prices.yaml` prices it; an unknown model is charged the most expensive row.

- The provider consoles carry the same cap (Anthropic Console → Limits; OpenAI → Billing limits; Google Cloud budget). The code refuses *before* a call, the provider refuses *regardless* of the code. Both are required and documented in the README.
- `GET /api/stats` shows cap, month-to-date, remaining and the recent ledger so spend is visible without opening a console.

# Evals

- Unit tests prove the code; evals measure the agent with real models. `evals/cases.yaml` is the set; `agent eval` is the runner; `evals/results/<tag>.{json,md}` is the committed evidence.
- Categories, each with at least three cases once the domain exists: `in_scope` (must answer, named tools must be called, key facts in `must_contain`), `off_topic` and `injection` (must refuse with the right status), `false_positive` (looks suspicious, must answer), `followup` (multi-turn via `prior_turns`).
- `--repeat N` runs each case N times: a case that passes some runs is *flaky* (exit 2), one that fails every run is *failed* (exit 1). A prompt or model change may not merge on exit 1.
- `--down <vendor>` drops a vendor from the chain to prove cross-vendor fallback end to end; the report records the simulated outage and which model served each run.
- Each report records models, guard, config version, cost and latency per run, so two reports can be compared by hand or diffed as JSON.
- Rule: any change to prompts, the chain, the guard threshold or the schemas is committed with the new report and a one-line comparison to the previous one in the commit message.
=== agent-os/standards/guardrails.md
# Guardrails

- Order: deterministic input checks (empty, too long, control characters, injection regexes) → decision model → answer model. The cheapest layer that can decide, decides.
- The decision model is TypeSafe Jev (`typesafe:jev-latest`) when `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` is set: typed questions (`Screening` fields), calibrated per-field confidence read from `provider_details["confidence"]`. Below `guard_confidence` or on any API error, `FallbackModel` sends the same question to Claude Haiku. Without a Jev key, Haiku screens alone.
- Policy lives in code: the model returns `in_scope` and `injection`; `Guard.screen` maps them to a label; `Service.ask` maps the label to a fixed refusal string. The model never writes refusal text.
- A refusal never reaches the answer model and never spends from the budget (the reservation is released).
- User text is data: the guard instructions say so, the answer instructions say so, and eval category `injection` proves it on every run. Category `false_positive` proves ordinary questions that contain words like "system" or "ignore" still pass.
- Logs record the guard decision and model per session prefix; the API response records `guardrail` only as the deciding layer's name, never the reasoning.

# Python style

- Errors are typed (`BudgetExceeded`, `InputRejection`) and surface as a `Turn.status`, never as a silent default.
- Async for anything that awaits a model; sync for pure code. The service is async end to end.
- `ruff check src tests` clean (E, F, I, B, UP). Line length 110.
- Comments: one line, at most 100 characters, only when the intent is not obvious from the code. Module docstrings say *why* the module exists in two or three lines. No essay docstrings; design lives in `docs/DESIGN.md` and the specs.
- Commit messages: `<type>: <what it does>` (`feat`, `fix`, `test`, `docs`, `chore`), one spec per feature commit, tests green before every commit.

This folder is a **private scratch reference**, never pushed. The real project is a new folder and a new session:

- Local: `C:\ai-projects\hubrisk`
- GitHub: public repo `ozeriyarin/hubrisk`, branch `main`, commit straight to main (solo repo)

## The brief (take-home, ~24 h, follow-up interview runs the agent live)

**Weather Risk Intelligence Agent.** A US logistics company runs regional distribution hubs; severe weather shuts
hubs down. Each year it funds resilience upgrades for a handful of hubs. Build an agent that helps analysts decide
which hubs are most exposed to weather disruption. Sample questions it must answer:

1. Which hubs in the Midwest are most exposed to winter disruption?
2. Compare Miami and Houston in terms of hurricane and flood exposure.
3. What percentage of days in Denver last year had snowfall?
4. Why is the Dallas hub's weather disruption risk high?

Must: public APIs for weather/hazard data; rank or compare hubs on a defined KPI; explain reasoning; conversational
follow-ups; **deterministic scoring, not only LLM output**; chat interface (voice = bonus); agent exposed through an
API the chat uses; **enforced JSON schema between LLM and code**; a small eval set and a way to run it; clear
assumptions, uncertainty and scoping. Bonus: scheduled or webhook alert when a hub's score changes.

Deliverables: source with run instructions; deploy to a URL preferred (Render); a short design doc covering system
architecture, repository structure, data storage choice; **and the full session with the AI agent (plan and all),
mandatory** → the session transcript is part of the repo. Consequences for the new session: no mention of other
projects, people, employers or memory notes; keep the conversation on this product; follow the process visibly.

Grading hint from the brief: clarity, reasoning and thoughtful design over completeness; narrow scope done well.

## Process: Agent OS v3, in this order, no code before its spec

1. `/plan-product` → `agent-os/product/{mission,roadmap,tech-stack}.md` (answer its questions from this file).
2. `/discover-standards` + `/index-standards` → `agent-os/standards/*.md` + `index.yml`.
3. Per feature: `/shape-spec` in plan mode → `agent-os/specs/<date>-<slug>/spec.md` with Goal, Scope, numbered
   **Acceptance criteria**, Design, Tasks. Every criterion gets a test `test_criterion_<n>_<slug>`; a spec-coverage
   test enforces it. Then code, `ruff`, `pytest`, eval report when prompts/models change, README/roadmap closeout, commit.
4. Commit messages `<type>: <what it does>`; tests green before every commit.

Base clone of Agent OS v3 is at `~/agent-os`; copy `~/agent-os/commands/agent-os/*.md` into `.claude/commands/agent-os/`.

Suggested spec order (one per roadmap version):
- `v0-platform`: model chain + retries + fallback, guard, budget, API, sessions, rate limits, eval runner, CI, Render.
- `v1-hubs-and-data`: hub registry, Open-Meteo archive ingest, NWS alerts/forecast client, Parquet snapshot, DuckDB.
- `v2-disruption-kpi`: the scoring engine and its tools.
- `v3-agent`: prompts, tools wired, schema, eval cases per category, first eval report.
- `v4-deploy`: Render live, verified, README section.
- `v5-alerts` (bonus): score-change webhook on a schedule. `v6-voice` (bonus): browser speech in the chat page.

## Product decisions already taken (confirm in /plan-product, do not re-debate)

- **KPI: expected disruption days per year, per hub and per hazard**, absolute and interpretable, computed from
  operational thresholds over daily history (snowfall ≥ X cm, wind gust ≥ Y km/h, precipitation ≥ Z mm, heat ≥ T°C,
  cold ≤ T°C), with a **year-to-year uncertainty band** (min/max or stdev across years) and a **5-year trend**.
  Overall score = weighted sum of hazard disruption-days, weights in a versioned YAML. Regions (Midwest, South, …)
  are a hub attribute so "Midwest hubs" is a filter, not a model guess. Hurricane/flood exposure can use FEMA NRI
  county data as a secondary signal if time allows; otherwise heavy-rain and gust days from history.
- **Data:** Open-Meteo archive API (daily, no key) for 2016–2025 history; **NOAA NWS API** (api.weather.gov, no key)
  for active alerts and the 7-day forecast per hub, powering "why is X high right now" and the alert bonus.
- **Storage: DuckDB over Parquet snapshots committed to the repo.** Ingest once locally, commit the Parquet; a deploy
  needs no re-ingest and Render's ephemeral disk does not matter. Runtime SQLite only for the spend ledger.
- 12–15 hubs across regions (e.g. Chicago, Minneapolis, Detroit, Columbus, Kansas City, Dallas, Houston, Miami,
  Atlanta, Denver, Phoenix, Los Angeles, Seattle, Newark, Memphis) with lat/lon, region, county FIPS in `config/hubs.yaml`.
- The LLM never produces a number; every figure comes from a tool. Answers are `AnswerOut` (status, answer,
  sources, limitations) validated by Pydantic AI.

## Stack decisions already taken

- Python 3.12, uv (`C:\Users\User\.local\bin\uv.exe`, add to PATH), `src/app/` layout, Typer CLI `agent serve|chat|eval`.
- **Pydantic AI 2.63** (`pydantic-ai-slim[anthropic,openai,google,typesafe,retries]`): `Agent(output_type=…)`,
  `FunctionToolset`, `UsageLimits(request_limit, cost_limit)`, `message_history` for memory.
- **Model chain** in `config/agent.yaml`: `anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5` → `anthropic:claude-haiku-5-5` →
  `openai:gpt-5.2` → `google-gla:gemini-2.5-flash`, through `FallbackModel(fallback_on=[ModelAPIError, truncated])`.
  Per-model HTTP retries with `AsyncHTTPX2TenacityTransport` (429/5xx/network, Retry-After aware, capped); vendor
  SDK retries **off** (`max_retries=0`); a model whose key is missing is skipped at startup with a log line.
  Note: Pydantic AI 2.x uses `httpx2`, and all-models-down raises `FallbackExceptionGroup`, not `ModelAPIError`.
- **Guard:** regex layer → `Screening(in_scope, injection)` answered by **TypeSafe Jev** (`typesafe:jev-latest`,
  native in Pydantic AI, confidence in `response.provider_details["confidence"]`) with `FallbackModel` to Haiku when
  Jev errors or any field confidence < 0.7. Policy in code; refusals are fixed strings; refusals spend nothing.
- **Budget:** SQLite ledger, monthly cap `BUDGET_USD`, reserve (BEGIN IMMEDIATE) → settle → release; cost from
  `result.usage.cost` (genai-prices) else `config/prices.yaml`; per-turn `cost_limit`; 20 req/IP/hour, 200/day.
- **API:** FastAPI `/health`, `POST /api/chat`, `GET /api/stats` (admin token), `DELETE /api/sessions/{id}`,
  static single-file chat page at `/`. In-memory sessions (1 h TTL, LRU 500), one asyncio lock per session.
- **Evals:** `evals/cases.yaml` (categories in_scope / off_topic / injection / false_positive / followup; fields
  expect, must_contain, must_not_contain, tools, prior_turns) → `agent eval --repeat N --tag T --down <vendor>` →
  `evals/results/T.{json,md}`; exit 0 pass / 1 fail / 2 flaky.
- **Tests:** pytest offline, `FunctionModel`/`TestModel` fakes, `httpx2.MockTransport`; `MODEL_MODE=test` runs the
  whole app keyless. CI: ruff + pytest + offline eval smoke. Deploy: `render.yaml` Blueprint, python runtime,
  `uv sync --frozen --no-dev`, `/health` probe, secrets as `sync: false`.
- Working scaffold of all of the above (55 tests green) is in **this folder**; lift modules into `hubrisk` only once

**How `test_spec_coverage.py` works**
- It globs `ROOT/agent-os/specs/*/spec.md` and skips any folder named in `UNIMPLEMENTED: set[str] = set()` (currently empty).
- It extracts the `## Acceptance criteria` section, matched case-insensitively and ending at the next `##` heading or the end of the file.

- For each number `n` it needs `def test_criterion_{n}_\w+` somewhere in the combined text of all `tests/test_*.py` files.
- The match is by number only, not by spec, so one `test_criterion_1_x` covers criterion 1 in every spec. Two specs sharing a number cannot be told apart.
